_evidence: 0x0040ad35 tests dword +0x2c of the 0x160-byte segment records at 0x008943a0 against 0x10 or 0x20 (chosen by the sign of byte 0x00868582), starting at [0x00866ecc]-0x580 (4 records back) and stepping back one record until a clear bit or until the pointer equals [0x00866f00]. Both pointers are record-aligned (records_008943a0: lap end 4..26, other end 0..24). When the start lies below the end pointer the original keeps walking below the array (it read record -1 at 0x0089426c and stops at the first clear bit); it never faults there, so instead of excluding those orders the +0x2c dwords of records -8..25 (0x008938cc + k*0x160) are all varied as full u32 (each test bit clear in half of the records, both loop exits common).
